# Momentum with a crash brake on TQQQ — development report

**Slug:** `momentum-crash-filter`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 (development only; 2024-2026 never used or
inspected)
**Harness:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute regular-session marks, next-open fills,
2% band, 1 bp headline; 5 bp and 10 bp sensitivity. Long-only, weights ≥ 0,
sum ≤ 1.
**Files:** `HYPOTHESIS.md` (pre-registration), `strategy.py`, `result.json`.

---

## Verdict

**Formal pass on the full-window bar, with a clear and honest qualification.**
At 1 bp the strategy makes **42.70% CAGR / 47.57% max DD / 1.005 Sharpe**,
versus the TQQQ bar of **36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82**. It still passes at 5 bp
(41.61% / 48.16% / 0.988) and 10 bp (40.26% / 48.88% / 0.967). The max DD is
below the "ideally < 60%" line at every cost level, and the Calmar ratio is
about twice TQQQ's.

The qualification: **the return edge is a crash-avoidance payoff, not broad
alpha.** The strategy wins 2020 (+57.8 pp vs TQQQ) and 2022 (+58.3 pp) and loses
every other calendar year, badly in 2019 (−80.7 pp) and 2023 (−65.0 pp). The
full-window CAGR wins because avoiding two 70–80% TQQQ drawdowns compounds.
Unlike `crash-early-warning`, the edge is not only 2020: ex-2020 CAGR is
**30.27%** versus TQQQ's **27.84%** on the same exclusion, because 2022 is also
avoided. But ex-2020-and-2022 CAGR is 41.55% versus TQQQ's 72.99%, so the
strategy is not an all-weather replacement for TQQQ.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **CAGR** | **42.70%** | **41.61%** | **40.26%** | 36.72% |
| **Max DD** | **47.57%** | **48.16%** | **48.88%** | 82.29% |
| **Sharpe** | **1.005** | **0.988** | **0.967** | 0.82 |
| **Calmar** (CAGR / DD) | **0.897** | **0.864** | **0.824** | 0.446 |
| Sortino | 1.414 | 1.390 | 1.360 | — |

| TQQQ weight (average) | 79.9% | 79.9% | 79.9% | 100% |

| Ending equity ($100k) | $1,709,441 | $1,607,961 | $1,489,540 | $1,175,283 |

The benchmark measured on the same 1-minute panel is 36.15% CAGR / 82.29% max
DD / 0.801 Sharpe; the task's reference bar is 36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82. The
candidate beats both. The `bt.stats` "exposure" field is 100% because BIL is an
asset; the economically relevant TQQQ exposure is **79.9% of sessions**.
Turnover is 746× start equity, higher than the pre-registered ~350× estimate
because every switch is a full-book trade; the 10 bp run still passes at 40.26%
CAGR, so the cost sensitivity is acceptable.

## 1. What the strategy does

At each session close, using QQQ daily bars through that close:

```
r20 = C_t / C_{t-20} - 1
r60 = C_t / C_{t-60} - 1
M   = (r20 > 0) or (r60 > 0)                     # momentum gate

DD20 = C_t / max(C_{t-19..t}) - 1
VA   = RV5 / RV20                                # 5-day / 20-day realised vol
R3   = ln(C_t / C_{t-3})                         # 3-day log return
CRASH = (DD20 < -8%) and ( (VA > 1.50) or (R3 < -6%) )

HI5 = max(C_{t-5..t-1})
```

State machine, evaluated at every close and filled at the next open:

- If defensive, re-enter TQQQ when `C_t >= HI5` **and** `r20 > 0`.
- Otherwise, go defensive on `CRASH`.
- Hold TQQQ when `M` is true and the book is not defensive; otherwise hold BIL.

The first 60 sessions (2016-01-04 → 2016-03-28) have no 60-session history in
the archive and are default-long TQQQ. The crash brake is active from session
20, when `DD20` and `VA` are defined. This is a real limitation, not a choice.

The momentum gate is deliberately loose ("either" horizon). Requiring both
horizons was tested on the daily screen and cut CAGR to about 22%: it re-enters
too late after a V-shaped recovery. Using TQQQ itself instead of QQQ for the
momentum signal was also much worse (about 22% CAGR on the daily screen):
3× daily returns are too noisy for a 20/60 gate. QQQ is the signal asset; TQQQ
is the implementation.

## 2. Yearly returns

Measured on the same 1-minute panel, year-end to year-end; the 2016 base is the
first session of the archive.

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | Difference |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | **+0.2%** | +19.9% | −19.6 pp |
| 2017 | +101.5% | +118.3% | −16.9 pp |
| 2018 | **−28.1%** | −19.6% | −8.5 pp |
| 2019 | +52.4% | +133.1% | **−80.7 pp** |
| 2020 | **+167.4%** | +109.6% | **+57.8 pp** |
| 2021 | +56.3% | +83.0% | −26.6 pp |
| 2022 | **−20.8%** | −79.1% | **+58.3 pp** |
| 2023 | +133.4% | +198.4% | **−65.0 pp** |

The shape is a crash hedge: it gives up 8.5–80.7 pp in the bull/choppy years
and earns it back in 2020 and 2022. It does not beat TQQQ in any other calendar
year. The full-window CAGR wins because the two crash years are the two largest
relative gains and they compound.

## 3. Drawdown and episode attribution

Peak-to-trough within the same calendar window, 1-minute marks:

| Episode | TQQQ max DD | Strategy max DD | Avoided | TQQQ return | Strategy return |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2018-08-30 → 2018-12-24 | −56.0% | −40.4% | **+15.7 pp** | −54.5% | −39.3% |
| 2020-02-20 → 2020-03-20 | −72.2% | −26.2% | **+46.0 pp** | −65.8% | −23.8% |
| 2021-11-22 → 2022-12-28 | −82.1% | −37.7% | **+44.4 pp** | −81.2% | −26.9% |
| 2023-01-01 → 2023-12-29 | −34.9% | −31.6% | +3.4 pp | +195.9% | +136.4% |

The full-period max DD is **47.57%**, peak **2018-01-29**, trough
**2019-01-23**. It is a 2018 event, not a 2020/2022 event: the strategy's two
big wins are precisely the two episodes where TQQQ's drawdown was worst.

The 2020 exit signal was on 2020-02-25 at QQQ 207.19 (−9.1% from the 20-session
high; TQQQ 10.44), filling at the next open; the re-entry signal was on
2020-04-06 (QQQ 189.45; TQQQ 6.11), also filling at the next open. On the actual
open-to-open fills (2020-02-26 → 2020-04-07), the defensive spell avoided a
−37.4% TQQQ move. The
2022 bear was handled by a sequence of spells: 2022-01-18 → 2022-02-24
(−25.1% TQQQ), 2022-04-14 → 2022-06-23 (−39.0%), 2022-08-29 → 2022-10-21
(−27.9%). The 2018 Q4 episode was only a partial success: the strategy avoided
15.7 pp but still lost 39.3%, because it re-entered the November rally and was
hit again.

### Defensive-spell statistics (daily marks)

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---:|
| Spells | 38 |
| Median / mean / max length | 6 / 10.6 / 48 sessions |
| Defensive sessions | 404 (20.1%) |
| Spells with TQQQ **up** (false alarms) | **65.8%** |
| Mean TQQQ move in down spells | **−13.5%** |
| Mean TQQQ move in up spells (cost) | **+7.1%** |

The 65.8% false-alarm rate is the honest number. The strategy works because the
right spells are much larger: four of the 38 spells avoided −25% to −39% of
TQQQ, while the average wrong spell cost 7.1%. The geometric asymmetry is what
matters: avoiding a −39% loss is worth 1.64×; missing a +7% gain costs 1.07×.
A handful of large avoided losses dominate many small missed rallies.

### Event study: the crash trigger is a tail filter, not a mean predictor

There are 11 crash triggers in 2,012 sessions (0.55%). Forward TQQQ returns:

| Horizon | Mean after crash | Mean all days | Negative share after | Negative share all | 10th pct after | 10th pct all | Min after | Min all |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 days | +6.4% | +2.0% | 36.4% | 36.0% | −16.6% | −14.1% | −19.3% | −57.5% |
| 20 days | +3.7% | +4.1% | 45.5% | — | **−34.1%** | **−18.1%** | **−50.3%** | −67.5% |

The crash state does **not** have a lower average forward return. It has a much
fatter left tail at 20 days: the 10th percentile is −34.1% versus −18.1%
unconditionally, and the minimum is −50.3%. That is the economic case for the
brake: it is a tail hedge, not a short signal. The 10-day window is too short to
see the full effect; the spell table above is the better attribution.

## 4. Robustness

### 4.1 Pre-registered 8-cell grid (daily marks)

One-at-a-time neighbours around the core; everything else fixed. The grid is a
plateau test, not a search for the best cell.

| # | Cell | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | TQQQ time |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | **core** (DD −8%, VA 1.50, loss −6%, re 5) | **42.30%** | 46.53% | 0.984 | 153 | 79.9% |
| 2 | dd early (−6%) | 38.09% | 45.88% | 0.932 | 149 | 78.1% |
| 3 | dd late (−10%) | 38.48% | 48.09% | 0.906 | 165 | 81.4% |
| 4 | vol tight (1.80) | 40.39% | 51.02% | 0.952 | 157 | 80.4% |
| 5 | loss tight (−4%) | **30.84%** | 55.68% | 0.817 | 161 | 78.4% |
| 6 | loss loose (−8%) | 43.97% | 46.53% | 0.996 | 157 | 80.3% |
| 7 | re-entry fast (3) | 43.73% | 49.04% | 0.996 | 153 | 80.3% |
| 8 | re-entry slow (7) | 38.90% | 49.98% | 0.941 | 149 | 78.9% |

**7 of 8 cells pass** the CAGR > 36.72% / DD < 82.29% bar, and all eight have
DD below 56%. The failure is the tight 4% 3-day-loss leg: it exits too often in
ordinary corrections and costs 11.5 pp of CAGR. The core sits in the middle of
the plateau (the seven passing cells are 38.1–44.0% CAGR and 45.9–51.0% DD; the
4% loss failure is 30.8% / 55.7%), not at the maximum. The 6%
3-day-loss threshold was fixed on the daily screen as a "sharp multi-day loss"
(roughly an 18% TQQQ move), not by maximising CAGR.

### 4.2 Wider neighbour table (daily marks)

| Variant | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **core** | 42.30% | 46.53% | 0.984 | 79.9% |
| momentum buffer −0.5% | **45.24%** | 44.01% | 1.021 | 80.9% |
| momentum buffer −1.0% | **47.09%** | 50.50% | 1.035 | 82.2% |
| momentum buffer −2.0% | 43.51% | 57.05% | 0.975 | 84.1% |
| momentum buffer +1.0% | 37.56% | 43.41% | 0.929 | 77.6% |
| drawdown window 15 | 42.30% | 46.53% | 0.984 | 79.9% |
| drawdown window 30 | 42.30% | 46.53% | 0.984 | 79.9% |
| re-entry 10 | 34.60% | 54.21% | 0.876 | 78.4% |
| re-entry 15 | 33.46% | 56.37% | 0.859 | 78.1% |
| re-entry 20 | 34.45% | 56.37% | 0.876 | 78.1% |
| no re-entry momentum (`r20>0`) | 33.11% | 51.37% | 0.833 | 81.8% |
| no crash brake | 34.69% | 51.37% | 0.837 | 83.4% |

The plateau is broad in the momentum-buffer direction: a small hysteresis band
**improves** CAGR to 45–47% with DD of 44–51% for the −0.5%/−1% cells. The
core's strict zero buffer is the conservative choice, not the maximum. The
re-entry speed is the more sensitive parameter: 10-day and slower re-entries
fall below the bar (33.5–34.6%), while 3 and 7 days both pass (43.7% and 38.9%).
The 5-day reclaim is the design choice that makes the V-shaped 2020 recovery
work. The drawdown window is inert at 15/20/30 because the volatility or
3-day-loss leg almost always occurs inside a >8% drawdown from the 20-day high;
the drawdown condition is a necessary gate but not the discriminating variable.

### 4.3 Component attribution (daily marks)

| Rule | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | TQQQ time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Momentum only (no crash) | 34.69% | 51.37% | 0.837 | 165 | 83.4% |
| Crash only (default long, 5-day reclaim) | 39.32% | **82.59%** | 0.867 | 65 | 94.0% |
| Crash only + `r20>0` re-entry | 38.22% | 72.54% | 0.877 | 45 | 89.1% |
| DD + 3-day loss (no vol leg) | **43.33%** | **43.56%** | 0.993 | 153 | 81.2% |
| DD + vol spike (no loss leg) | **43.78%** | 46.53% | 0.988 | 157 | 80.5% |
| Loss only | 41.53% | 52.38% | 0.973 | 157 | 80.1% |
| Vol only | 31.91% | 41.13% | 0.836 | 277 | 71.1% |
| **Core (momentum + crash)** | **42.30%** | **46.53%** | **0.984** | 153 | 79.9% |

This is the clearest evidence that the combination is the strategy:

- Momentum alone misses the CAGR bar (34.69%).
- Crash alone misses the drawdown point (82.59%, essentially TQQQ's): the
  default-long overlay re-enters every bear-market rally and gets hit again.
- The momentum gate is what avoids the slow 2022 bear; the crash brake is what
  avoids the fast 2020 crash. Neither alone does both.
- Both crash legs work: DD+loss (43.33% / 43.56%) and DD+vol (43.78% / 46.53%)
  are close to the core. The two confirmations are complementary, not redundant.

### 4.4 Placebo (500 circular shifts, daily marks)

The full TQQQ/BIL state vector is shifted by a random amount, preserving the
exact spell lengths and the 20.1% defensive exposure. This tests whether the
timing matters or whether the result is just "be out of TQQQ 20% of the time".

| | Observed | Placebo mean | Placebo p5 | Placebo p95 | Observed percentile |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 42.30% | 27.50% | 12.88% | 45.30% | **92.0th** |
| Max DD | 46.53% | 77.09% | 69.23% | 86.35% | **0.2th** |
| Sharpe | 0.984 | 0.706 | — | 0.931 | **97.2th** |

The DD reduction is far outside the random-timing distribution: only 1 of 500
shifts has a lower max DD, and only 0.8% have a DD below 60%. The CAGR edge is
weaker: 16.8% of random shifts also beat the 36.72% bar, and the observed CAGR
is only the 92nd percentile. This is consistent with the ex-year evidence: the
**risk reduction is the robust part; the CAGR pass is a crash payoff.** The
placebo's joint "CAGR > bar and DD < 82.29%" share is 16.4%, so the loose DD bar
alone is not a high hurdle; the < 60% DD result is the discriminating outcome.

### 4.5 Cut tests (causality)

Rebuilding the signal on data truncated at the session close gives **zero**
weight differences before the cut:

| Cut | Bars compared | Weight differences |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2018-12-21 | 291,156 | 0 |
| 2020-03-12 | 409,752 | 0 |
| 2022-09-13 | 655,277 | 0 |

The signal uses only data through the decision close. No look-ahead. The first
60 sessions are the only period without a full 60-session momentum history, and
they are explicitly default-long TQQQ.

### 4.6 Ex-year fragility

Daily marks for this decomposition (the 1-minute headline is in the first
table; the 1-minute ex-2020 result is 30.27% / 46.53% / 0.821).

| Sample | Strategy CAGR | Strategy DD | Strategy Sharpe | TQQQ CAGR | TQQQ DD | TQQQ Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Full 2016–2023 | 42.30% | 46.53% | 0.984 | 35.98% | 81.68% | 0.80 |
| Ex-2020 | **30.27%** | 46.53% | 0.821 | **27.84%** | 81.68% | 0.711 |
| Ex-2022 | 55.02% | 46.53% | 1.167 | **77.75%** | 69.89% | 1.242 |
| Ex-2020 & 2022 | 41.55% | 46.53% | 1.020 | **72.99%** | 57.97% | 1.321 |

The pre-registered falsifier **ex-2020 CAGR ≤ TQQQ ex-2020 CAGR is not
triggered**: 30.27% > 27.84%. That is a genuine improvement over
`crash-early-warning`, whose ex-2020 CAGR was 24.7% versus TQQQ's 27.8%. The
edge is a two-crash-year edge (2020 and 2022), not a one-year edge. But without
both crash years the strategy badly lags TQQQ on CAGR (41.6% vs 73.0%) while
still cutting the DD. It is a crash hedge, not an all-weather alpha source.

## 5. Where it fails

1. **Strong, crash-free bull markets.** 2019 (+52.4% vs +133.1%), 2021 (+56.3%
   vs +83.0%) and 2023 (+133.4% vs +198.4%) are the problem. The momentum gate
   exits during ordinary corrections and re-enters higher; the strategy gives
   up 27–81 pp in those years. If the 2024-2026 holdout is a strong bull with no
   meaningful drawdown, the strategy will lag TQQQ.
2. **Choppy bear markets.** 2018 is the failure: the strategy lost 28.1% versus
   TQQQ's 19.6% and its full-period max DD (47.57%) is the 2018-01 → 2019-01
   path. The 5-day reclaim buys the first bear rally, which is often a trap. The
   2018 Q4 episode avoided only 15.7 pp of a 56.0 pp TQQQ decline.
3. **Warm-up.** The 1-minute archive starts 2016-01-04, so the first 60 sessions
   have no 60-session momentum history and are default-long TQQQ. 2016 finished
   +0.2% versus TQQQ +19.9%; the January 2016 drawdown is effectively
   unprotected by the momentum gate (the crash brake is active from session 20).
4. **False alarms.** 65.8% of defensive spells had TQQQ up, average cost +7.1%.
   The strategy tolerates this because the right spells are much larger (four
   avoided −25% to −39%), but a run of false alarms in a bull market is a
   material drag.
5. **The crash trigger is not a mean-return predictor.** Forward 10-day TQQQ
   returns after a trigger average +6.4% versus +2.0% unconditionally; the
   20-day 10th percentile is what improves (−34.1% vs −18.1%). The filter is a
   tail hedge; it will look wrong most of the time in a V-shaped recovery.
6. **Holdout arithmetic.** With the dev total at 17.09× over 7.98 years, beating
   a 37.54% full 2016-2026 CAGR requires roughly a **23.9% CAGR in the
   2024-2026 holdout** (about 1.83× over 2.8 years). That is plausible if the
   holdout contains a meaningful drawdown, but not guaranteed in a strong,
   calm bull. The dev cushion is real but not infinite.

## 6. Relation to existing work

This is a standalone strategy, not a re-parameterisation of an existing one:

- **`research/new/crash-early-warning`:** default 100% TQQQ, de-risks on a
  3-component score (vol acceleration + drawdown acceleration + gap stress)
  with B mandatory, re-enters on a 10-day high. This strategy has a **20/60
  momentum gate**, no gap-stress component, no drawdown-velocity term, a 5-day
  reclaim, and a 3-day-loss leg. It is not default long: it stands aside on
  negative momentum even without a crash. The state paths and the yearly tables
  are different (crash-early-warning 2020 +218%, 2022 −33%; this strategy 2020
  +167%, 2022 −21%).
- **`research/new/fast-trend-vol`:** 20/50-day EMA trend + vol target + daily
  and intraday crash brakes. No EMA, no vol target, no intraday override; the
  trend signal is total-return momentum.
- **`research/new/vol-of-vol-timing`:** vol-of-vol / Parkinson range risk state.
  No range estimator, no vol-of-vol, no V-recovery re-risk.
- **`research/new/cross-asset-momentum`:** dual momentum across QQQ/SPY/BIL.
  Single signal asset (QQQ), no cross-asset ranking.
- **`research/agents2/drawdown-regime` / `revisit/drawdown-regime`:** exits on
  the level of QQQ drawdown from a 52-week high on top of the 165-day SMA + 4%
  stop. No SMA, no stop; 20-session drawdown plus a fast-stress confirmation.
- **`research/agents2/stop-reentry-recovery`, `vol-scaled-crash-stop`:** stops.
  This has no stop.
- **`research/agents2/overnight-crash-filter`:** overnight-only with a 20-day
  vol filter. Holds all day.
- **`research/agents2/ml-crash-overlay-winner`:** walk-forward logistic
  classifier on a 165-day SMA base. Deterministic rule, no ML, no slow MA.
- **`research/agents2/event-risk-overlay`:** FOMC/CPI/OpEx calendar events. No
  calendar.
- **`research/new/ml-regime-v2`:** walk-forward ML with momentum signs
  (60/100/150). No ML, 20/60 only.

No code or parameters were copied. The only shared component is `research/bt.py`
for fills and marks, as required.

## 7. Honest verdict

**Pass on the letter of the bar:** 42.70% CAGR > 36.72%, 47.57% max DD < 82.29%
(and < 60%), 1.005 Sharpe > 0.82, at 1/5/10 bp. The signal is causal (cut tests
identical), the pre-registered grid is a plateau (7/8 cells pass, all DDs below
56%), and the drawdown reduction is not a random-exposure artifact (0.2th
percentile vs 500 placebo shifts).

**But do not read it as an all-weather replacement for TQQQ.** The return edge
is a 2020/2022 crash-avoidance payoff: the strategy loses every other calendar
year, badly in 2019 and 2023. Ex-2020 CAGR still beats TQQQ (30.3% vs 27.8%),
which is better than `crash-early-warning`, but ex-2020-and-2022 CAGR is 41.6%
versus TQQQ's 73.0%. The CAGR edge is only the 92nd percentile against random
timing, and 16.8% of random shifts also beat the bar; the DD reduction is the
robust, decisive result (0.2th percentile, only 0.8% of placebos below 60% DD).

The strategy's correct use is as a **crash-hedged trend sleeve on a TQQQ
core**, not as a standalone all-weather alpha strategy. For the lead's one-shot
holdout, it is a reasonable candidate: it has a 42.7% dev CAGR, a 47.6% DD, a
genuine two-crash-year edge, and a causal, interpretable signal. It needs about
a 23.9% holdout CAGR to beat the full 2016-2026 37.54% bar; that is likely if
2024-2026 contains a real drawdown, and at risk if it is a calm, strong bull.

**Bottom line:** a real, interpretable momentum-with-crash-brake strategy that
clears the development bar with a 47.6% max DD (35 pp below TQQQ's), at the

# Momentum with a crash brake on TQQQ — pre-registration

**Slug:** `momentum-crash-filter`
**Status:** frozen before the final 1-minute development run.
**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 only. The 2024-01-02 → 2026-10-23
holdout is not loaded, inspected or used for selection by this study; every
`bt.panel` call ends at 2023-12-29.
**Bar:** TQQQ 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 is **36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82
Sharpe** on 1-minute marks. Pass = dev CAGR > 36.72% and max DD < 82.29%
(ideally < 60%). A lower-CAGR but much better Sharpe/Calmar result is reported
as risk-adjusted, not as a pass.

This is a standalone strategy. It does not use the 165-day QQQ SMA, the 4%
intraday stop, the old drawdown-regime exit, the old event-risk overlay, the ML
crash classifier, the overnight-only structure, or the EMA/vol-target structure
of `fast-trend-vol`. It has no stop-loss and no intraday override.

---

## 1. Mechanism

TQQQ is a 3× daily-reset Nasdaq-100 fund. Two empirical regularities do the
work:

1. **Momentum persists at the 1–3 month horizon.** QQQ total return over the
   prior 20 and 60 sessions is positively autocorrelated at these horizons
   (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012). A positive
   20/60-session return is a simple, causal proxy for "the equity risk premium
   is currently being paid". Holding TQQQ while either horizon is positive
   keeps the strategy in the long bull legs (2017, 2019, 2020H2, 2021, 2023)
   without a slow 100–200-day moving average.
2. **Crashes are partly predictable from their own dynamics.** Volatility
   clusters (Engle 1982; Bollerslev 1986), and a fast drawdown that is
   accompanied by a volatility spike or a sharp 3-day loss is more likely to
   continue than a quiet drift down. For a 3× fund the asymmetry is large: a
   20% QQQ drawdown is roughly a 45–60% TQQQ drawdown because of the daily
   reset and the path-dependent variance drag (Avellaneda & Zhang 2010; Cheng &
   Madhavan 2009). Cutting the first part of such an episode is worth far more
   than the CAGR given up by occasionally re-entering late.

The strategy is therefore a **trend-following core with an explicit crash
brake**, not a default-long overlay:

- The **momentum gate** decides whether TQQQ is an eligible asset. It is
  deliberately loose ("either 20 or 60 sessions positive") because TQQQ's
  recoveries are violent and a strict "both positive" gate re-enters too late.
- The **crash brake** overrides the gate. It requires a *fast drawdown from a
  20-session high* **and** at least one fast-stress confirmation (a 5/20-day
  volatility spike or a sharp 3-day loss). A slow grind lower does not trigger;
  a one-day gap without a prior drawdown does not trigger.
- **Re-entry** is a price-confirmation rule: a close at or above the prior
  5-session high **and** a positive 20-session return. This is the
  "stabilisation/reclaim" leg. It is faster than waiting for the 60-session
  momentum to turn positive, which is what allows the strategy to participate
  in V-shaped recoveries such as April 2020.

Why this can beat TQQQ: TQQQ's 2016–2023 CAGR is high because the bull years
compound strongly, but the 2018 Q4, 2020 COVID and 2022 bear episodes account
for the 82% drawdown. If the brake avoids the majority of the 2020 and 2022
declines while the momentum gate keeps most of the bull years, the compounded
result can be higher with a much lower tail. The strategy does not need to beat
TQQQ every year; it needs to beat it over the full window with a smaller
drawdown.

## 2. Exact rules

All signals are computed at the close of session `t` from QQQ regular-session
daily bars (open, close), using data through `t` only. Weights are set at that
close and filled at the **next session's open** (`bt.run`, 2% band, next-open
fills). No full-sample statistics are used.

Let `C_t` be the QQQ close of session `t`.

```
r20_t    = C_t / C_{t-20} - 1
r60_t    = C_t / C_{t-60} - 1
r_t      = ln(C_t / C_{t-1})
RV5_t    = stdev(r_{t-4..t})  * sqrt(252)
RV20_t   = stdev(r_{t-19..t}) * sqrt(252)
VA_t     = RV5_t / RV20_t
DD20_t   = C_t / max(C_{t-19..t}) - 1
R3_t     = ln(C_t / C_{t-3})
HI5_t    = max(C_{t-5..t-1})          # prior 5 sessions, excludes t
```

**Momentum state** (eligible to hold TQQQ):

```
M_t = (r20_t > 0) or (r60_t > 0)
```

The first 60 sessions (2016-01-04 → 2016-03-28) have no 60-session history in
the 1-minute archive. The strategy is default-long TQQQ during that warm-up;
the crash brake is active from the first session in which `DD20` and `VA`/`R3`
are defined (20 sessions). This is a real limitation, not a choice.

**Crash trigger** (evaluated at the close, overrides `M_t`):

```
CRASH_t = (DD20_t < -0.08) and ( (VA_t > 1.50) or (R3_t < -0.06) )
```

**State machine** (`off` = defensive):

```
off_0 = False
for t = 0..n-1:
    if off_{t-1}:
        if (C_t >= HI5_t) and (r20_t > 0):     # reclaim + short momentum
            off_t = False
    elif CRASH_t:
        off_t = True
    else:
        off_t = False

TQQQ weight_t = 1 if (M_t and not off_t) else 0
BIL  weight_t = 1 - TQQQ weight_t
```

Execution: the target for session `t` is written on the 15:59 bar and fills at
the next session's 09:30 open. Every other bar in session `t` carries the
position already held. No intraday signal, no stop, no short, no leverage above
100%.

### Pre-registered core parameters

| Parameter | Value | Role |
|---|---:|---|
| `mom_fast` | 20 sessions | fast momentum horizon |
| `mom_slow` | 60 sessions | slow momentum horizon |
| `mom_buf` | 0.0% | strict positive momentum (no buffer) |
| `dd_win` | 20 sessions | fast drawdown lookback |
| `dd_t` | −8.0% | QQQ drawdown from 20-session high |
| `va_t` | 1.50 | RV5 / RV20 volatility-spike threshold |
| `loss_t` | −6.0% | 3-day QQQ log-return crash threshold |
| `reentry` | 5 sessions | prior-high reclaim window |
| `re_mom` | yes | re-entry also requires r20 > 0 |
| `defensive` | BIL | cash proxy |

The thresholds are round, mechanism-driven values, fixed after a **daily-mark
screen** and before the final 1-minute run. The screen is not the headline; the
1-minute run below is the single final evaluation. The volatility threshold
1.50 is a 50% spike in 5-day versus 20-day realised vol; the 8% drawdown is
roughly a 24% TQQQ drawdown; the 6% 3-day QQQ loss is roughly an 18% TQQQ loss.

## 3. Pre-registered 8-cell grid

One-at-a-time neighbours around the core, everything else fixed. The grid is a
**plateau test**, not a search for the best cell.

| # | Cell | Change |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **core** | — |
| 2 | dd early | `dd_t = −6.0%` |
| 3 | dd late | `dd_t = −10.0%` |
| 4 | vol tight | `va_t = 1.80` |
| 5 | loss tight | `loss_t = −4.0%` |
| 6 | loss loose | `loss_t = −8.0%` |
| 7 | re-entry fast | `reentry = 3` |
| 8 | re-entry slow | `reentry = 7` |

Additional diagnostics (not part of the 8-cell selection grid): momentum
buffers −0.5%/−1%/−2%, `dd_win` 15/30, the no-crash variant, the momentum-only
variant, the crash-only variant, the component legs (dd+loss, dd+vol, loss only,
vol only), and a 10/15/20-day re-entry horizon.

## 4. Expected effect (written before the final 1-minute run)

- 1 bp: CAGR 39–44%, max DD 42–50%, Sharpe 0.92–1.02.
- 5 bp / 10 bp: CAGR 40–43% / 38–41%; the pass should survive 10 bp because
  turnover is low (~150 fills, ~350× start equity over eight years).
- TQQQ exposure: 78–82% of sessions; BIL 18–22%.
- Daily-return correlation to TQQQ: 0.65–0.75.
- Yearly shape: strong 2020 and 2022 relative performance; weak 2016 (no
  warm-up), 2018 (choppy bear with false alarms), 2019/2021/2023 below TQQQ
  because the momentum gate and the re-entry lag give up part of the upside.
- The edge is expected to be concentrated in crash avoidance: ex-2020 CAGR
  should still be positive and above TQQQ's ex-2020 CAGR (about 27.8% on daily
  marks), but it will be well below the headline.

## 5. Falsifiers (written before the final run)

The hypothesis fails if any of these is true:

1. **Headline failure:** dev 1 bp CAGR ≤ 36.72% or max DD ≥ 82.29%.
2. **No plateau:** fewer than 6 of the 8 pre-registered grid cells pass, or the
   core collapses by more than ~5 pp CAGR versus the daily screen (42.3%).
3. **No timing value:** a circular-shift placebo that preserves the exact
   exposure-spell lengths and exposure fraction matches the observed CAGR and
   drawdown (observed CAGR percentile < 90, or more than 20% of placebo draws
   above the 36.72% bar).
4. **Look-ahead:** truncating the 1-minute panel at 2018-12-21, 2020-03-12 or
   2022-09-13 changes any weight before the cut.
5. **Only 2020:** ex-2020 CAGR ≤ TQQQ's ex-2020 CAGR. (The strategy is allowed
   to earn a large part of its edge in crash years, but not all of it. Ex-2022
   and ex-both are reported as diagnostics, not pass criteria, because TQQQ
   without its worst year is not a meaningful bar.)
6. **Old strategy in disguise:** the result is reproduced by the 165-day SMA +
   4% stop, the old drawdown-regime exit, or the `crash-early-warning`
   default-long composite. The state path and exposure profile are reported so
   this can be checked.

## 6. Relation to existing work (checked before writing this)

- `research/new/crash-early-warning`: default 100% TQQQ; de-risks on a
  3-component score (vol acceleration + drawdown acceleration + gap stress)

- `research/new/fast-trend-vol`: 20/50-day EMA trend + volatility target +

- `research/new/vol-of-vol-timing`: vol-of-vol / Parkinson range risk state.

- `research/new/cross-asset-momentum`: dual momentum across QQQ/SPY/BIL.

- `research/agents2/drawdown-regime` and `research/revisit/drawdown-regime`:

- `research/agents2/stop-reentry-recovery`: post-4%-stop re-entry. **No stop.**
- `research/agents2/vol-scaled-crash-stop`: ATR-scaled 4% stop. **No stop.**
- `research/agents2/overnight-crash-filter`: overnight-only with a 20-day vol

- `research/agents2/ml-crash-overlay-winner`: walk-forward logistic classifier

- `research/agents2/event-risk-overlay`: FOMC/CPI/OpEx calendar events. **No

- `research/new/ml-regime-v2`: walk-forward ML with momentum signs (60/100/150).

No code or parameters are copied from any of them.

## 7. Diagnostics that will be reported

- 1-minute headline at 1/5/10 bp; daily screen for comparison.
- Yearly returns, the 2018 Q4 / 2020 COVID / 2022 bear attribution, and the
  max-DD peak/trough.
- All 8 pre-registered grid cells, plus the wider sensitivity table.
- Component rules (momentum only, crash only, dd+loss, dd+vol, loss only, vol

## 1. What the strategy does

At each session close, using QQQ daily bars through that close:

```

M   = (r20 > 0) or (r60 > 0)                     # momentum gate

```

- If defensive, re-enter TQQQ when `C_t >= HI5` **and** `r20 > 0`.
- Otherwise, go defensive on `CRASH`.
- Hold TQQQ when `M` is true and the book is not defensive; otherwise hold BIL.

the archive and are default-long TQQQ. The crash brake is active from session
20, when `DD20` and `VA` are defined. This is a real limitation, not a choice.

The momentum gate is deliberately loose ("either" horizon). Requiring both
horizons was tested on the daily screen and cut CAGR to about 22%: it re-enters
too late after a V-shaped recovery. Using TQQQ itself instead of QQQ for the
momentum signal was also much worse (about 22% CAGR on the daily screen):
3× daily returns are too noisy for a 20/60 gate. QQQ is the signal asset; TQQQ
is the implementation.

"""Momentum with a crash brake on TQQQ.

Hold TQQQ while QQQ 20- or 60-session total-return momentum is positive.
Override to BIL when a fast drawdown from a 20-session high is confirmed by
either a 5/20-day volatility spike or a sharp 3-day loss.  Re-enter TQQQ on a
close at or above the prior 5-session high with positive 20-session momentum.

Development window only: 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29.
The 2024-2026 holdout is never loaded by this file.

Run from the repository root:

    python research/new/momentum-crash-filter/strategy.py

It writes result.json next to this file.  Fills are delegated to
research/bt.py (next-open, 2% band, slippage on traded notional).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

START = "2016-01-04"
END = "2023-12-29"
SYMBOLS = ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL")

TQQQ = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
BIL = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
BARS_PER_YEAR_1M = 252 * 390
BARS_PER_YEAR_1D = 252
START_EQUITY = 100_000.0
BAR_CAGR = 0.3672
BAR_DD = 0.8229

# Frozen core.  Every key is overridable for the pre-registered grid.
PARAMS = dict(
    mom_fast=20,
    mom_slow=60,
    mom_buf=0.0,
    dd_win=20,
    dd_t=-0.08,
    va_t=1.50,
    loss_t=-0.06,
    reentry=5,
    re_mom=True,
    warm=max(20, 60),
    min_periods=20,
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# signals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _daily_bars(ts, o, c):
    """Aggregate a daily or 1-minute panel to session opens/closes."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    return dates, o[first], c[last], first, last


def _features(daily_close, p):
    """Causal daily features from QQQ closes through session t."""
    qc = daily_close[:, 0]
    n = len(qc)
    s = pd.Series(qc)
    r = np.diff(np.log(qc), prepend=np.log(qc[0]))

    rv5 = pd.Series(r).rolling(5, min_periods=5).std().to_numpy() * np.sqrt(252.0)
    rv20 = (
        pd.Series(r)
        .rolling(20, min_periods=p["min_periods"])
        .std()
        .to_numpy()
        * np.sqrt(252.0)
    )
    va = rv5 / rv20

    dd20 = qc / s.rolling(p["dd_win"], min_periods=p["dd_win"]).max().to_numpy() - 1.0
    r3 = pd.Series(np.log(qc)).diff(3).to_numpy()
    hi5 = s.rolling(p["reentry"], min_periods=p["reentry"]).max().shift(1).to_numpy()

    r20 = qc / s.shift(p["mom_fast"]).to_numpy() - 1.0
    r60 = qc / s.shift(p["mom_slow"]).to_numpy() - 1.0
    return qc, r20, r60, va, dd20, r3, hi5


def _daily_targets(daily_close, p):
    """State machine at session closes; weights execute at the next open."""
    qc, r20, r60, va, dd20, r3, hi5 = _features(daily_close, p)
    n = len(qc)
    crash = (dd20 < p["dd_t"]) & ((va > p["va_t"]) | (r3 < p["loss_t"]))
    crash = np.nan_to_num(crash.astype(float)).astype(bool)

    wd = np.zeros((n, 3))
    state = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int8)
    trigger = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int8)
    off = False
    for t in range(n):
        if off:
            reclaim = np.isfinite(hi5[t]) and qc[t] >= hi5[t]
            mom_ok = (not p["re_mom"]) or (np.isfinite(r20[t]) and r20[t] > 0)
            if reclaim and mom_ok:
                off = False
        elif crash[t]:
            off = True
            trigger[t] = 1
        momentum_on = (r20[t] > p["mom_buf"]) or (r60[t] > p["mom_buf"])
        if t < p["warm"]:
            momentum_on = True
        state[t] = 1 if (momentum_on and not off) else 0
        wd[t] = TQQQ if state[t] else BIL
    return wd, state, crash, trigger


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None):
    """Build the (n, 3) target-weight matrix for a daily or 1-minute panel.

    `weights[i]` is the target set from bar i's close and is executed at
    bar i+1's open by bt.simulate.  For a 1-minute panel the session-close
    decision is written on the 15:59 bar, so it fills at the next 09:30 open;
    every other bar in a session carries the position already held.
    """
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    dates, do, dc, first, last = _daily_bars(ts, o, c)
    wd, state, crash, trigger = _daily_targets(dc, p)
    n = len(ts)
    if len(first) == n:  # daily panel: one bar per session
        return wd

    w = np.empty((n, 3))
    for d in range(len(first)):
        prev = wd[d - 1] if d > 0 else TQQQ
        w[first[d] : last[d] + 1] = prev
        w[last[d]] = wd[d]
    return w


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# metrics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _yearly(eq, bench, ts):
    """Calendar-year returns from the first bar of the slice."""
    es = pd.Series(eq, index=ts)
    bs = pd.Series(bench, index=ts)
    ye = es.groupby(ts.date).last()
    yb = bs.groupby(ts.date).last()
    y0 = pd.Series(ye.values, index=pd.to_datetime(ye.index)).groupby(lambda x: x.year).last()
    b0 = pd.Series(yb.values, index=pd.to_datetime(yb.index)).groupby(lambda x: x.year).last()
    out = {}
    years = list(y0.index)
    first_bench = float(bench[0])
    for k, y in enumerate(years):
        base = START_EQUITY if k == 0 else float(y0[years[k - 1]])
        bbase = first_bench if k == 0 else float(b0[years[k - 1]])
        out[int(y)] = {
            "strategy": float(y0[y] / base - 1.0),
            "benchmark": float(b0[y] / bbase - 1.0),
        }
    return out


def _metrics(ts, o, c, w, cost_bps, bars_per_year, start=START):
    res = bt.run(ts, o, c, w, start, band=0.02, slippage_bps=cost_bps)
    st = bt.stats(res, bars_per_year)
    i = bt.start_index(ts, start)
    b = bt.benchmark(c[i:, 1], ts[i:], bars_per_year)
    eq = res["equity"]
    rr = np.diff(eq) / eq[:-1]
    rt = np.diff(c[i:, 1]) / c[i:-1, 1]
    corr_bar = float(np.corrcoef(rr, rt)[0, 1]) if len(rr) > 2 else float("nan")

    es = pd.Series(eq, index=ts[i:])
    de = es.groupby(ts[i:].date).last().pct_change().dropna()
    dt = pd.Series(c[i:, 1], index=ts[i:]).groupby(ts[i:].date).last().pct_change().dropna()
    corr_daily = float(de.corr(dt)) if len(de) > 2 else float("nan")

    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    dd = eq / peak - 1.0
    j = int(np.argmin(dd))
    pk = int(np.argmax(eq[: j + 1]))

    ww = w[i:]
    return {
        "cost_bps": float(cost_bps),
        "cagr": float(st["cagr"]),
        "total_return": float(st["total_return"]),
        "max_drawdown": float(st["max_drawdown"]),
        "sharpe": float(st["sharpe"]),
        "sortino": float(st["sortino"]),
        "volatility": float(st["volatility"]),
        "exposure_any_asset": float(st["exposure"]),
        "tqqq_weight_avg": float(ww[:, 1].mean()),
        "time_in_tqqq": float((ww[:, 1] > 0.5).mean()),
        "time_in_bil": float((ww[:, 2] > 0.5).mean()),
        "fills": int(st["fills"]),
        "turnover_x_start_equity": float(st["turnover"]),
        "ending_equity": float(st["ending_equity"]),
        "corr_tqqq_bar": corr_bar,
        "corr_tqqq_daily": corr_daily,
        "max_dd_peak": str(pd.Timestamp(ts[i + pk]).date()),
        "max_dd_trough": str(pd.Timestamp(ts[i + j]).date()),
        "benchmark": {
            "cagr": float(b["cagr"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(b["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(b["sharpe"]),
            "volatility": float(b["volatility"]),
        },

def _public(m):
    return {k: v for k, v in m.items() if not k.startswith("_")}


def _episodes(ts, eq, bench, episodes):
    out = []
    for a, b in episodes:
        m = (ts >= pd.Timestamp(a, tz="America/New_York")) & (
            ts <= pd.Timestamp(b, tz="America/New_York")
        )
        e, t = eq[m], bench[m]
        if len(e) < 2:
            continue
        dd_e = float((e / np.maximum.accumulate(e) - 1.0).min())
        dd_t = float((t / np.maximum.accumulate(t) - 1.0).min())
        out.append(
            {
                "start": a,
                "end": b,
                "tqqq_max_dd": dd_t,
                "strategy_max_dd": dd_e,
                "avoided_dd_pp": 100.0 * (dd_e - dd_t),
                "tqqq_return": float(t[-1] / t[0] - 1.0),
                "strategy_return": float(e[-1] / e[0] - 1.0),
            }
        )
    return out


def _ex_year(m, drop_years):
    """Compound daily returns excluding calendar years, then recompute stats."""
    eq = m["_equity"]
    dates = m["_dates"]
    de = pd.Series(eq, index=dates).groupby(dates.date).last()
    dr = de.pct_change().dropna()
    keep = ~np.isin(pd.to_datetime(dr.index).year, list(drop_years))
    r = dr[keep].to_numpy()
    curve = START_EQUITY * np.cumprod(1.0 + r)
    years = len(r) / 252.0
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(curve)
    return {
        "excluded_years": list(drop_years),
        "cagr": float((curve[-1] / START_EQUITY) ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0),
        "max_drawdown": float(-(curve / peak - 1.0).min()),
        "sharpe": float(np.mean(r) / np.std(r, ddof=0) * np.sqrt(252.0)),
        "n_days": int(len(r)),
    }


def _ex_year_bench(ts, bench, drop_years):
    de = pd.Series(bench, index=ts).groupby(ts.date).last()
    dr = de.pct_change().dropna()
    keep = ~np.isin(pd.to_datetime(dr.index).year, list(drop_years))
    r = dr[keep].to_numpy()
    curve = START_EQUITY * np.cumprod(1.0 + r)
    years = len(r) / 252.0
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(curve)
    return {
        "excluded_years": list(drop_years),
        "cagr": float((curve[-1] / START_EQUITY) ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0),
        "max_drawdown": float(-(curve / peak - 1.0).min()),
        "sharpe": float(np.mean(r) / np.std(r, ddof=0) * np.sqrt(252.0)),

def _component_weights(daily_close, p, use_mom, crash_mode, re_mom):
    """Component rules for attribution (daily marks)."""
    qc, r20, r60, va, dd20, r3, hi5 = _features(daily_close, p)
    n = len(qc)
    if crash_mode == "both":
        crash = (dd20 < p["dd_t"]) & ((va > p["va_t"]) | (r3 < p["loss_t"]))
    elif crash_mode == "dd_loss":
        crash = (dd20 < p["dd_t"]) & (r3 < p["loss_t"])
    elif crash_mode == "dd_vol":
        crash = (dd20 < p["dd_t"]) & (va > p["va_t"])
    elif crash_mode == "loss":
        crash = r3 < p["loss_t"]
    elif crash_mode == "vol":
        crash = va > p["va_t"]
    elif crash_mode == "none":
        crash = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    else:
        raise ValueError(crash_mode)
    crash = np.nan_to_num(crash.astype(float)).astype(bool)

    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    off = False
    for t in range(n):
        if off:
            reclaim = np.isfinite(hi5[t]) and qc[t] >= hi5[t]
            mom_ok = (not re_mom) or (np.isfinite(r20[t]) and r20[t] > 0)
            if reclaim and mom_ok:
                off = False
        elif crash[t]:
            off = True
        on = True
        if use_mom:
            on = (r20[t] > p["mom_buf"]) or (r60[t] > p["mom_buf"])
            if t < p["warm"]:
                on = True
        w[t] = TQQQ if (on and not off) else BIL
    return w

def _placebo(ts, o, c, w, n_draws=500, seed=20261127):
    state = (w[:, 1] > 0.5).astype(np.int8)
    n = len(state)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cagr, dd, sharpe = [], [], []
    for _ in range(n_draws):
        shift = int(rng.integers(20, n - 20))
        ss = np.roll(state, shift)
        ww = np.where(ss[:, None] == 1, TQQQ, BIL)
        st = _run_daily(ts, o, c, ww)
        cagr.append(st["cagr"])
        dd.append(st["max_drawdown"])
        sharpe.append(st["sharpe"])
    core = _run_daily(ts, o, c, w)
    arr_c = np.array(cagr)
    arr_d = np.array(dd)
    arr_s = np.array(sharpe)
    return {
        "n_draws": n_draws,
        "method": "circular shift of the full TQQQ/BIL state vector; preserves spell lengths and exposure",
        "observed": {
            "cagr": float(core["cagr"]),
            "max_drawdown": float(core["max_drawdown"]),
            "sharpe": float(core["sharpe"]),
        },
        "placebo": {
            "cagr_mean": float(arr_c.mean()),
            "cagr_p05": float(np.percentile(arr_c, 5)),
            "cagr_p95": float(np.percentile(arr_c, 95)),
            "dd_mean": float(arr_d.mean()),
            "dd_p05": float(np.percentile(arr_d, 5)),
            "dd_p95": float(np.percentile(arr_d, 95)),
            "sharpe_mean": float(arr_s.mean()),
            "sharpe_p95": float(np.percentile(arr_s, 95)),
        },
        "observed_percentile": {
            "cagr": float(100.0 * np.mean(arr_c < core["cagr"])),
            "max_drawdown": float(100.0 * np.mean(arr_d < core["max_drawdown"])),
            "sharpe": float(100.0 * np.mean(arr_s < core["sharpe"])),
        },
        "share_placebo_cagr_above_bar": float(100.0 * np.mean(arr_c > BAR_CAGR)),
        "share_placebo_dd_below_60pct": float(100.0 * np.mean(arr_d < 0.60)),
        "share_placebo_joint_pass": float(
            100.0 * np.mean((arr_c > BAR_CAGR) & (arr_d < BAR_DD))
        ),
    }


def _cut_tests(ts, o, c, w, cuts):
    out = {}
    for cut in cuts:
        stamp = pd.Timestamp(cut, tz="America/New_York").replace(hour=15, minute=59)
        j = int(ts.searchsorted(stamp, side="right"))
        if j <= 0 or j >= len(ts):
            out[cut] = {"error": "cut outside panel"}
            continue
        wt = build_weights(ts[:j], o[:j], c[:j])
        m = min(len(wt), j)
        diff = np.flatnonzero(
            (w[:m, 1] != wt[:m, 1]) | (w[:m, 2] != wt[:m, 2])
        )
        out[cut] = {
            "bars_compared": int(m),
            "weight_differences": int(len(diff)),
            "first_difference_bar": int(diff[0]) if len(diff) else None,
            "identical": bool(len(diff) == 0),
        }
    return out


def _spell_stats(daily_open, daily_close, w):
    """Descriptive attribution of defensive spells on daily marks.

    `off` is set at the close of day t and filled at the next open, so the
    TQQQ move actually avoided runs from open[t+1] to open[exit+1].
    """
    o = daily_open[:, 1]
    off = w[:, 2] > 0.5
    n = len(off)
    starts = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(off.astype(np.int8)) == 1) + 1
    ends = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(off.astype(np.int8)) == -1)
    lens, moves = [], []
    for s in starts:
        cand = ends[ends >= s]
        entry = min(int(s) + 1, n - 1)
        if len(cand) == 0:
            exit_px = o[-1]
            length = n - int(s)
        else:
            e = int(cand[0])
            exit_px = o[min(e + 2, n - 1)]
            length = e - int(s) + 1
        lens.append(int(length))
        moves.append(float(exit_px / o[entry] - 1.0))
    moves = np.array(moves)
    return {
        "n_spells": int(len(lens)),
        "median_length_sessions": float(np.median(lens)) if lens else None,
        "mean_length_sessions": float(np.mean(lens)) if lens else None,
        "max_length_sessions": int(np.max(lens)) if lens else None,
        "share_spells_tqqq_up": float(np.mean(moves > 0)) if len(moves) else None,
        "mean_tqqq_move_down_spells": float(np.mean(moves[moves < 0])) if np.any(moves < 0) else None,
        "mean_tqqq_move_up_spells": float(np.mean(moves[moves > 0])) if np.any(moves > 0) else None,
        "total_sessions_defensive": int(off.sum()),
        "share_sessions_defensive": float(off.mean()),
    }


def _event_study(daily_close, trigger):
    qc = daily_close[:, 0]
    n = len(qc)
    tc = daily_close[:, 1]
    tbool = np.asarray(trigger).astype(bool)
    fwd10 = np.full(n, np.nan)
    fwd10[:-10] = tc[10:] / tc[:-10] - 1.0
    fwd20 = np.full(n, np.nan)
    fwd20[:-20] = tc[20:] / tc[:-20] - 1.0
    ok10 = np.isfinite(fwd10)
    ok20 = np.isfinite(fwd20)
    return {
        "crash_triggers": int(tbool.sum()),
        "crash_share": float(tbool.mean()),
        "fwd10_tqqq_mean_after_crash": float(np.nanmean(fwd10[tbool & ok10])) if np.any(tbool & ok10) else None,
        "fwd10_tqqq_mean_all": float(np.nanmean(fwd10[ok10])),
        "fwd10_tqqq_negative_share_after_crash": float(np.nanmean(fwd10[tbool & ok10] < 0)) if np.any(tbool & ok10) else None,
        "fwd10_tqqq_negative_share_all": float(np.nanmean(fwd10[ok10] < 0)),
        "fwd10_tqqq_min_after_crash": float(np.nanmin(fwd10[tbool & ok10])) if np.any(tbool & ok10) else None,
        "fwd10_tqqq_p10_after_crash": float(np.nanpercentile(fwd10[tbool & ok10], 10)) if np.any(tbool & ok10) else None,
        "fwd10_tqqq_min_all": float(np.nanmin(fwd10[ok10])),
        "fwd10_tqqq_p10_all": float(np.nanpercentile(fwd10[ok10], 10)),
        "fwd20_tqqq_mean_after_crash": float(np.nanmean(fwd20[tbool & ok20])) if np.any(tbool & ok20) else None,
        "fwd20_tqqq_mean_all": float(np.nanmean(fwd20[ok20])),
        "fwd20_tqqq_negative_share_after_crash": float(np.nanmean(fwd20[tbool & ok20] < 0)) if np.any(tbool & ok20) else None,
        "fwd20_tqqq_min_after_crash": float(np.nanmin(fwd20[tbool & ok20])) if np.any(tbool & ok20) else None,

        "fwd20_tqqq_p10_all": float(np.nanpercentile(fwd20[ok20], 10)),
    }
